content: 1. Settings for Service Delivery: Health services can be delivered in facility-based settings, such as hospitals, health clinics, and general practice offices, or in community-based settings, including drop-in centers, mobile clinics, outreach teams, and community support groups. These services are often targeted in cities or regions of epidemiological importance. 2. Global Reporting Platforms: Key platforms for monitoring health data include the Global AIDS Monitoring system, the WHO Global Hepatitis Reporting System, and tools for validating hepatitis C elimination progress. 3. Indicator for Safe Injections in Healthcare Facilities: This indicator evaluates the implementation of policies ensuring safe injection practices. Tools developed by WHO and the Safe Injection Global Network Alliance have been used successfully for national surveys on injection safety. 4. Global Target for Injection Safety: The global target is to achieve 100% safe healthcare injections. 5. Screening of Blood Units for Bloodborne Diseases: This assesses the implementation of policies ensuring all blood donations are screened for these infections. The global target is 100% screening of blood units. 6. Diagnosis of Chronic Hepatitis B: The global target is for at least 90% of people with chronic hepatitis B to be diagnosed. Data sources include medical records, laboratory registers, and national biomarker surveys. 7. Diagnosis of Chronic Hepatitis C: The global target is for at least 90% of people with chronic hepatitis C to be diagnosed. Data sources include clinical records, laboratory registers, and biomarker surveys. 8. Initiation of Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis B: WHO recommends treatment for all eligible individuals to achieve viral suppression. The global target is for at least 80% of eligible individuals to initiate treatment. 9. Current Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis B: This indicator helps monitor progress in providing ongoing care and achieving viral suppression. 10. Initiation of Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis C: WHO recommends treatment for all individuals with chronic hepatitis C. The global target is for at least 80% of diagnosed individuals to initiate treatment. 11. Annual Follow-Up for Untreated Chronic Hepatitis B: For individuals with chronic hepatitis B who are not initiating treatment, annual monitoring for disease progression, including ALT and HBV DNA levels, is recommended. 12. Attrition from Antiviral Therapy for Chronic Hepatitis B: This indicator tracks those who have died, stopped treatment, or been lost to follow-up. Retention and attrition analysis are essential for program management. 13. Cure Rate for Chronic Hepatitis C: This indicator reflects the effectiveness of hepatitis C treatment programs. Each of these indicators is critical for monitoring and evaluating progress toward global health targets for hepatitis prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.
